findings.title: Practical AI coding agent setup and workflow guide
findings.qualifying_date_basis: Article page shows Guides By Ivern AI Team July 4, 2026.
findings.factual_summary: The guide walks through API-key setup, terminal agent installation, bug-fix, feature, refactoring, and multi-agent workflows. It emphasizes reviewing AI changes, supplying clear context, keeping context windows clean, using version control, and routing different task types to different agents or models.
findings.why_it_matters: The local wiki can use this as a practice-level signal that AI coding adoption guidance is converging on explicit setup gates, bounded workflow types, context hygiene, review discipline, and version-control boundaries rather than open-ended prompting.
findings.local_practice_implication: Treat setup, context packaging, review, and version-control expectations as first-class adoption instructions for AI-assisted development workflows.
findings.routing_note: Do not duplicate product comparisons or benchmark claims locally; route product and model coverage upstream.

findings.title: Agent platform engineering reference architecture
findings.factual_summary: The guide describes production agent platforms as layered systems that separate orchestration, model inference, tools, memory, retrieval, control plane, and runtime responsibilities. It frames persistent state, discoverable tools, delegated identity, observability, auditability, and rollback as platform concerns for non-deterministic agent workloads.
findings.why_it_matters: The local wiki already tracks agent platform boundaries; this source reinforces that coding-agent infrastructure should be documented as operating architecture with explicit ownership for memory, tools, identity, telemetry, and policy.
findings.local_practice_implication: Future ingest can strengthen pages on agent-platform boundaries, trace evidence, delegated identity, and control-plane versus runtime responsibilities.
findings.routing_note: Keep platform and protocol encyclopedia coverage upstream; retain only the local operating architecture implication.

findings.title: On-premise AI code review compliance guide
findings.visible_date: Published on July 4, 2026; Last Updated on July 4, 2026
findings.qualifying_date_basis: Article page shows both published and last-updated dates on July 4, 2026.
findings.factual_summary: The guide frames on-premise AI code review as a deployment choice for organizations whose compliance, security, data residency, sovereignty, or intellectual-property requirements rule out SaaS processing. It compares self-hosted, private-cloud, and air-gapped deployment variants and discusses when custom code-review agents are warranted.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a practice-level signal for AI code review adoption: review quality is not the only selection criterion; source-code location, audit controls, deployment model, and compliance mapping can decide whether AI review is usable at all.
findings.local_practice_implication: Code-review governance pages should treat data residency, source-code exposure, auditability, and air-gapped operation as review-tool acceptance gates.
findings.routing_note: Do not create local vendor comparison pages; upstream owns product and standards background.

findings.title: Compliance-as-code pull request checks
findings.qualifying_date_basis: Article page shows Publication Date: July 4, 2026.
findings.factual_summary: The article reports on Qodo's compliance-as-code framing: encode regulatory and security policies such as hardcoded-secret bans, protected-route RBAC, and idempotent payment retries as automated pull-request checks instead of relying on manual documentation and delayed audits.
findings.why_it_matters: This supports local practice around lifecycle review gates and regression repair: compliance requirements should become executable or reviewable PR evidence so AI-generated changes face the same policy checks as human-authored changes.
findings.local_practice_implication: Future synthesis can connect AI-assisted coding to policy-as-test and PR-level compliance evidence, especially for generated patches that must not bypass normal governance.
findings.routing_note: Qodo and regulatory background remain upstream-owned; keep the local lens on PR checks and compliance evidence.

findings.title: Context-aware AI code review selection criteria
findings.qualifying_date_basis: Article page shows Mesrai Team July 4, 2026.
findings.factual_summary: The guide argues that AI code review should understand repository-wide architecture rather than only isolated diffs. Its evaluation criteria include architectural context, Git-provider workflow integration, actionable feedback, customization to team standards, and review latency.
findings.why_it_matters: The local wiki can use this as evidence for code-review eval rubrics that measure retrieval depth, architectural context, actionability, and latency separately from generic product availability.
findings.local_practice_implication: Code-review eval pages can distinguish whole-repository context, isolated-diff analysis, committable suggestions, team-standard customization, and latency budget.
findings.routing_note: Vendor rankings and product details belong upstream; local use is the review-practice criteria.

findings.title: Enterprise ban of Claude Code over security classification
findings.qualifying_date_basis: Article page shows Posted: 9:32 AM PDT - July 4, 2026, which is inside the cutoff window.
findings.factual_summary: TechCrunch reports that Alibaba will ban employees from using Claude Code starting July 10 and classify it as high-risk software, while Anthropic already prohibits Chinese companies and their foreign-owned entities from using its models. The report ties the action to concerns about unauthorized access, distillation, and hidden user-identification behavior in a version of Claude Code.
findings.why_it_matters: The downstream lesson is not an entity update about Alibaba or Anthropic; it is that AI coding tools can become enterprise-restricted software when telemetry, jurisdiction, data-transfer, or model-access controls are unclear.
findings.local_practice_implication: Governance pages should preserve a tool-risk review path that covers vendor terms, telemetry, hidden enforcement mechanisms, jurisdictional policy, and approved internal alternatives before broad team rollout.
findings.routing_note: The companies, products, and regional-policy background are upstream-owned; local synthesis should focus on enterprise AI coding tool approval practice.

findings.title: Desktop file-agent permission and audit model
findings.qualifying_date_basis: Article page shows Jul 3, 2026. Search result and blog index place the item inside the cutoff window.
findings.factual_summary: The article treats desktop file agents as permissioned local-file workflows rather than autonomous coworkers. It emphasizes selected-folder access, operation-specific approval, reviewable trails, derived-output folders, explicit uncertainty questions, and audit records showing what the agent read, changed, and the user approved.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a useful bridge between coding-agent controls and broader team adoption: non-code file agents still need workspace scoping, review UX, reversible outputs, and durable audit evidence.
findings.local_practice_implication: Application-pattern and governance pages can generalize coding-agent permission patterns to desktop/file agents: read-only inputs, work and output folders, edit previews, and operation-specific approvals.
findings.routing_note: Product strategy and model lineup details are upstream-owned; retain only the file-agent control pattern.

findings.title: Agent adoption requires workflow redesign
findings.qualifying_date_basis: Newsletter archive title and search result show Saturday, July 4, 2026.
findings.factual_summary: The digest summarizes an argument that enterprise workflows often are not designed for agents because data is fragmented, legacy systems are inaccessible, and institutional knowledge is not documented. It also flags the compliance conversation triggered by rapid AI coding tool deployment.
findings.why_it_matters: This supports the local operating-model rule that agent adoption is workflow redesign plus governance, not tool insertion. AI-assisted development practices should identify missing context, inaccessible systems, and undocumented institutional knowledge before scaling agents.
findings.local_practice_implication: Adoption pages can treat fragmented knowledge and inaccessible systems as blockers that must be turned into context sources, tools, or documented workflows before agent rollout.
findings.routing_note: Company and executive coverage is upstream-owned; local use is the adoption and operating-model implication.
